summary: SPAN oversubscription at CORE-SW-01 Gi1/0/48 causes 42.26% loss before NDR (1.73 Gbps mirrored into 1 Gbps SPAN destination) plus 4.10% drops at NDR eth1; NDR receives only ~57% of intended traffic, severely degrading detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: CORE-SW-01 SPAN destination Gi1/0/48 is oversubscribed: 18,557,040 packets (1.73 Gbps) mirrored from Gi1/0/1 must egress a 1 Gbps SPAN destination port. Switch discarded 7,842,840 packets on output (42.26% lost, average load 100% of 1 Gbps, bursts higher). Downstream NDR eth1 additionally discarded 439,680 packets it did receive (4.10% lost) as capture interface could not keep up.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions and full payload on 10G port but receives only ~57% of traffic. ~42% of flows/packets never arrive plus additional ingest drops cause missed detections, broken flow reassembly, incomplete Zeek/Suricata logs and blind spots for lateral movement and exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN destination drops by design when mirrored rate exceeds destination capacity and cannot handle bursts. Passive TAP provides lossless out-of-band copy independent of switch resources and preserves both directions. Feed TAP via packet broker with adequate aggregation/buffering to the NDR's 10G port to eliminate the 42% SPAN loss and reduce downstream tool drops.
